standard_prerequisites.name: Properness with finite fibres in a neighbourhood, and the algebraic criterion in codimension one
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Cohomology of Schemes, label coherent-lemma-proper-finite-fibre-finite-in-neighbourhood (proof line 2543); Algebra, label algebra-lemma-finite-in-codim-1 (proof line 2553)
standard_prerequisites.use: The first reduces the statement to the finiteness of the fibre over the point, and the second provides the algebraic criterion giving finiteness over a neighbourhood in the one-dimensional case.

core_obligations: Reduce to finiteness of the fibre: by the properness criterion it suffices to prove that the fibre over the given point is finite (proof lines 2538-2544).
Go affine and cover the source: replace the target by an affine open and use quasi-compactness of the proper morphism to cover the source by finitely many affine opens (proof lines 2545-2549).

Apply the algebraic criterion: each of the resulting ring maps is an injective finite type homomorphism of domains with finite extension of fraction fields between Noetherian rings, and the criterion in codimension one gives finiteness over a neighbourhood (proof lines 2549-2553).
proof_roadmap: Reduction to a finite fibre (proof lines 2538-2544).
Affine reduction and finite affine cover (proof lines 2545-2549).
Algebraic criterion in codimension one (proof lines 2549-2553).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that a proper dominant morphism of integral schemes with finite extension of function fields is finite over a neighbourhood of any codimension one point of the target (statement lines 2523-2536, tag 02RG-adjacent). The proof notes that the statement follows from a general version over varieties, then gives a direct argument: it reduces to finiteness of the fibre over the point by a properness criterion, goes affine and covers the source by finitely many affine opens, and applies the algebraic criterion for finiteness in codimension one. The reduction and the algebraic translation are the substance, so the claim is H2.
